# OfflineShelf: full text

Source: https://offlineshelf.ahmershah.dev
Author: Syed Ahmer Shah (https://ahmershah.dev)
Contact: support@ahmershah.dev
License: code MIT; Wikipedia content in exports CC BY-SA 4.0
Status: in development, launching February 2027

## What it is

OfflineShelf builds Wikipedia reading lists for places without internet. Picking a few thousand good articles out of millions is the hard part of offline Wikipedia: the lists have to be reproducible, combinable and kept up to date. OfflineShelf is a small, self-hostable tool for that step.

## Builders

1. Category: every article (namespace 0) in a category and its subcategories, down to a depth limit of 5. Loops in the category tree are detected.
2. Wikidata: a SPARQL query against the Wikidata Query Service (up to 10,000 characters, 60 second timeout). Items are mapped to articles on the chosen wiki through sitelinks.
3. Pasted titles: up to 20,000 titles. Redirects are resolved and missing pages are reported.
4. Pageviews: the top N (up to 1,000) most-read articles of a month from the Wikimedia REST API.

Lists can target any language edition of Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia content projects (Wiktionary, Wikibooks, Wikinews, Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikiversity, Wikivoyage).

## Combinations

Union, intersection and difference of up to ten lists, for example "Physics minus Biographies". Cycles between lists are refused. A combination rebuilds when one of its source lists gets a new version.

## Builds, versions and schedules

Builds never run inside a web request. Each build is a background job with a status: queued, building, ready or failed. Network errors are retried with backoff. Each successful build is stored as a new version with the articles added and removed since the previous one. A failed build never replaces the last good version. Lists can rebuild monthly.

## Exports

- TSV: title, page ID and revision ID.
- Static HTML bundle: Parsoid HTML of each article, local links rewritten, with an attribution page.
- ZIM (stretch goal): a single file that Kiwix opens, for small lists.

Downloads are streamed and expire after seven days.

## Principles

- Titles, not text: only titles and IDs are stored.
- Attribution built in: every export carries the CC BY-SA 4.0 notice.
- Polite to Wikimedia: one identified User-Agent with a contact address, maxlag on every request, backoff when servers are busy.
- Yours to host: MIT licensed, one Docker Compose file.

## Privacy

Stored: your email address, an Argon2id hash of your password, and your list settings. One HttpOnly session cookie, 14 days. No analytics, advertising, tracking or third-party resources. Wikimedia APIs are called from the server, not the browser.

## API

JSON under /api/v1, errors as RFC 9457 problem details. Unsafe requests need the session cookie and the X-CSRF-Token header from GET /api/v1/auth/csrf.

- GET /api/v1/health
- GET /api/v1/auth/csrf
- POST /api/v1/auth/register, /auth/login, /auth/logout, /auth/logout-everywhere
- GET /api/v1/auth/me
- GET, POST /api/v1/lists
- GET, DELETE /api/v1/lists/{id}
- POST /api/v1/lists/{id}/build (202, version queued; 409 if a build is active)
- GET /api/v1/lists/{id}/versions, /versions/{v}, /versions/{v}/articles

Builds move queued, building, then ready or failed. Network errors with Wikimedia are retried after 1, 5 and 15 minutes. Rate limits: 300 requests a minute per IP; sign-in 10 a minute per IP and per email; builds 20 an hour.

## Self-hosting

Docker Compose runs nginx, the Flask API, an RQ worker, MariaDB 11.4 and Redis. Requirements: Docker 24+, about 2 GB RAM, outbound HTTPS to Wikimedia. Install: clone the repository, copy .env.example to .env, set OFFLINESHELF_SECRET_KEY and the MariaDB passwords, run docker compose up -d --build. Settings use the OFFLINESHELF_ environment prefix.

## Security

Argon2id password hashing, per-session CSRF tokens plus same-origin checks, HttpOnly SameSite cookies (Secure and __Host- prefixed in production), a per-request CSP nonce with strict-dynamic, rate limits at the edge and in the app, owner-scoped queries, a Wikimedia host allow list, non-root read-only containers. Report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub security advisories or support@ahmershah.dev. security.txt: /.well-known/security.txt

## Contact

Email support@ahmershah.dev. Bugs and features: GitHub issues. The maker: https://ahmershah.dev

## FAQ

What does OfflineShelf export? A TSV file of titles, page IDs and revision IDs, and a static HTML bundle of the articles with attribution. ZIM export for Kiwix is planned for small lists.

Does OfflineShelf copy Wikipedia articles into its database? No. It stores titles and IDs only.

Which wikis can I build lists from? Any language edition of Wikipedia, and the other Wikimedia content projects.

What happens when a scheduled rebuild fails? The last good version stays current, the failure is recorded, and the next rebuild tries again.

Is OfflineShelf free and open source? Yes, MIT licensed and self-hostable with Docker Compose.

Wikipedia is a trademark of the Wikimedia Foundation. OfflineShelf is an independent project and is not endorsed by or affiliated with the Foundation.
